title: Old Gold Comedy Theater
paragraphs: Single-season sponsored anthology hosted by Harold Lloyd, compressing Hollywood comedy films into half-hour radio adaptations.
The run breaks into several distinct periods: Single sponsored season (October 29, 1944 to June 10, 1945) on [[org|org.acb290b0843b31ec|Blue Network]].

Names that turn up again and again in the surviving run include Harold Lloyd (host), Carl Hoff (music director), Bob Williams (announcer), [[person|herbert-marshall|Herbert Marshall]] (host and performer), Ben Grauer (announcer), Tom Drake (performer), and Alan Young (performer).
Across its run, the surviving broadcasts are tied to [[org|org.acb290b0843b31ec|Blue Network]], [[org|org.4798d1172deaae2c|Armed Forces Radio Service]], and [[org|org.66865a83f6609315|KFI]].

The stories often return to Hollywood film-to-radio adaptation, comedy and comic misunderstanding, romance, courtship and marriage, mistaken identity, deception and social performance, money, jobs and social class, and show business, performance and publicity.

The show also sits in a wider radio history that includes Hollywood comedy adapted for sponsored radio, Old Gold cigarette sponsorship and agency packaging, Harold Lloyd radio-host experiment, and Near-complete preservation from the Harold Lloyd estate.

If you are following the same actors and creative circles, related programs worth opening next include [[show|lux-radio-theatre|Lux Radio Theatre]], [[show|screen-directors-playhouse|Screen Directors Playhouse]], [[show|duffys-tavern|Duffy's Tavern]], [[show|yours-truly-johnny-dollar|Yours Truly, Johnny Dollar]], and [[show|academy-award-theater|Academy Award Theater]].
